page: Microsoft Azure M32ps_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture, managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 512.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is not included, with GPU resources set to zero.

Storage configuration on the M32ps_v4 relies entirely on external attached storage, as no local disk space is bundled. The instance supports Premium Storage integration for remote block volumes. Network interfaces do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external IP assignment or private routing for network connectivity.

With its high memory-to-vCPU density on an energy-efficient ARM platform, this server offers a cost-effective operational profile for architectures where memory footprint dominates compute demands. Because there is no ephemeral local storage, all persistent and scratch data must traverse network-attached storage, which introduces remote disk latency considerations.

Workloads best suited for the M32ps_v4 include large in-memory databases, distributed caches, enterprise enterprise-resource planning systems, and large-scale data analytics pipelines that require substantial RAM capacity on ARM-native environments.
